A number becomes useful when you know what was measured and which unit expresses it. Length, mass and time describe different quantities; their units let another person interpret a recorded value. The same object can have different numerical values when expressed in different units. Keeping the number and unit together makes comparisons meaningful.

A plan can change as the team learns: some projects begin with stable requirements, while others need repeated adjustments. The useful question is what must happen next for this particular outcome.
